extracted.intended_audience: Recording Academy voting members, submitters (labels/content owners/producers/artists), and Awards Department staff
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards governing GRAMMY nominations, credit corrections, voting integrity, recognition (nominee/winner/certificate) and category-specific eligibility for awards and statuettes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credit change documentation (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: When requesting changes in credits, the submitter must provide required documentation including an affidavit verifying the change request is true, reason for the change, updated (final) label copy, and confirmation that credits have been updated across DSPs as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit changes through the GRAMMY Credit and Nomination Corrections portal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline for credit corrections before the telecast (two-week window)
rubrics_metrics.description: After the nomination’s announcement, submitters may request changes in the original credits within two weeks after the announcement, providing specified documentation and fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required items: formal statement from head of label/content owner/producer detailing inaccuracies or omissions and steps to correct; notarized statement from the artist where applicable; updated final label copy or credit list approved by content owner/producer; call sheets or studio logs proving additional persons worked on the recording and their roles where applicable; confirmation that credits have been updated across DSPs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee for adding names (pre-telecast and within-one-year requests)
rubrics_metrics.description: There will be a fee of $200 per added name to be paid in advance by the party requesting the changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to credit additions requested within the two-week post-announcement window and for requests made within one year after the telecast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline for credit corrections after the telecast (one-year)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a deadline of one year from the date of the telecast to make requests to the Awards Department for crediting changes/additions to nominated or winning albums; requirements are the same as the pre-telecast/short-window requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitters must provide the same documentation (formal statement by label/content owner/producer, notarized artist statement where applicable, updated label copy, call sheets/studio logs, fee, confirmation of DSP updates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests after one-year require Executive Committee approval
rubrics_metrics.description: After the one-year deadline, any request for changes must be made to the Executive Committee of the Board of Trustees of the Recording Academy; the requester must provide all necessary documents to show proof of claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consideration is at the sole discretion of the Executive Committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenges to GRAMMY Award entitlement process
rubrics_metrics.description: Any challenge to a final entitlement decision by the Awards Department must be made in writing and addressed to the Executive Committee of the Recording Academy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Executive Committee can investigate, consider, and decide the challenge, acting with the power of the Board of Trustees; its decision is final and will be communicated in writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final voting confidentiality and tabulation
rubrics_metrics.description: After nomination announcements, final ballots are made available to current Voting Members to select winners; all ballots (including special committees) are tabulated confidentially by an independent accounting firm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Results of final voting are sealed and not known until the day of the GRAMMY Awards when Deloitte delivers sealed envelopes with winners' names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescindment of GRAMMY policy
rubrics_metrics.description: If a GRAMMY Award is withdrawn after presentation, no award is given in that Category for that year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The GRAMMY process does not produce a ranked result with a winner and ordered runners-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of voting integrity (general principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Recording Academy requires that the GRAMMY Awards process be led in a fair and ethical manner and that Voting Members make choices solely based on the artistic and technical merits of eligible recordings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities that oppose the guidelines may lead to corrective actions, including disqualification of entries; members who enable vote solicitation may face suspension or termination of membership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voter Code of Conduct — independent merit-based voting
rubrics_metrics.description: Voters shall not allow their choices to be suggested, directed or influenced by anything other than their own analysis of merit, including personal friendships, company loyalties, regional preferences, or sales volume/popularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voter Code of Conduct — no exchange for votes
rubrics_metrics.description: Voters shall not accept money or anything of value in exchange for votes, access to other members (member lists and contact information are confidential), submission of materials for GRAMMY consideration, or any other membership privilege.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voter Code of Conduct — prohibition on voting agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Voters shall not enter into any agreements or understandings on how to vote, including but not limited to 'Voting Blocs' (groups agreeing to vote together) and 'Vote Trading' (offering to vote in exchange for another’s vote).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of Voting Blocs include voters affiliated with a particular record label, management company, or linked through social media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bloc voting corrective authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The Academy reserves the right to establish guidelines for its independent accountants to take confidential corrective action on behalf of the Academy as they deem appropriate regarding bloc voting or other issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: For Your Consideration (FYC) campaign rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Academy has codified Rules and Policies governing For Your Consideration campaigning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitters and campaigners must follow the Academy's FYC Rules and Policies (referenced on the Academy website).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of GRAMMY Nominee
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals who are eligibly credited on a GRAMMY-nominated recording for a nomination-eligible role are GRAMMY Nominees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominees receive an invitation to the GRAMMY Awards, information about Nominee ticket(s), a GRAMMY Nominee medallion and Nominee Certificate. Those who worked on a nominated project in a role that is not GRAMMY-nominated may say they 'worked on a GRAMMY-nominated project' but are not Nominees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of GRAMMY Winner (Statuette)
rubrics_metrics.description: Roles listed under Statuette are the GRAMMY Award winners on the winning projects and receive a GRAMMY Award statuette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list of winners includes the Nominees on the winning project as well as other roles recognized with statuettes (e.g., eligible producers, engineers and mixers who worked on more than 50% of playing time of winning albums in certain album categories). Additional winners are compiled and audited after the telecast; these winners are contacted and receive awards (but not necessarily Nominee tickets/mementos).

rubrics_metrics.name: Achievement Certificate eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals on a GRAMMY-winning recording whose roles are listed under Certificate receive an Achievement Certificate from the Academy after the telecast but are not GRAMMY Nominees or GRAMMY winners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These individuals can say they 'worked on a GRAMMY-winning project'. Participation Certificates are also available for purchase for roles not otherwise recognized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 1 — Record Of The Year (nominee/statuette/certificate roles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominee: Artist(s) & Producer(s), Engineer/Mixer(s), Mastering Engineer(s), if other than Artist(s). Statuette: Artist(s) & Producer(s), Engineer/Mixer(s), Mastering Engineer(s), if other than Artist(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 2 — Album Of The Year (nominee/statuette/certificate roles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominee: Artist(s) including Featured Artist(s), Songwriter(s) of new material, Producer(s), Recording Engineer(s), Mixer(s) & Mastering Engineer(s) with greater than 20% playing time on the album. Statuette: Artist(s) including Featured Artist(s), Songwriter(s) of new material, Producer(s), Recording Engineer(s), Mixer(s) & Mastering Engineer(s) with greater than 20% playing time on the album.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 3 — Song Of The Year (nominee/statuette/certificate roles)

rubrics_metrics.description: Nominee: Principal Artist(s) with significant contributing performances, and/or in-studio Producer(s) of a majority of the tracks on the album; up to two album Producers and Music Supervisors in certain circumstances. Statuette: Producer(s) & Engineer/Mixer(s) with less than 50% playing time; Mastering Engineer(s), if other than Artist(s); Immersive roles as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For albums largely of pre-existing masters, up to two album Producers and up to two Music Supervisors per criteria; for largely new recordings, awards to Principal Artist(s) with significant contributions and up to three Producers (possible fourth on appeal) and up to two Music Supervisors; Engineer/Mixer(s) of greater than 50% playing time of newly recorded material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 72 — Score Soundtrack For Visual Media (film & television) (nominee/statuette/certificate roles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominee & Statuette: Composer(s) of new material. Additional Statuette roles: Composer(s) of new material, Producer(s) & Engineer/Mixer(s) of greater than 50% playing time on the album.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publisher, Producer(s) & Engineer/Mixer(s) with less than 50% playing time of newly recorded material; Mastering Engineer(s) if other than Artist(s); Immersive roles as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 73 — Score Soundtrack For Video Games And Other Interactive Media (nominee/statuette/certificate roles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominee & Statuette: Composer(s) of new material. If more than one composer is listed, a minimum of 33% playing time will be required. Statuette: Composer(s) of new material, Music Producer(s) & Engineer/Mixer(s); 33% playing time rule applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a composer has a separate production team the 33% applies to that team's Music Producer(s) and Engineer(s)/Mixer(s). Certificates to Composer, Producer(s) & Engineer(s) of less than 33% if other than artist. Immersive roles as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 74 — Song Written For Visual Media (nominee/statuette/certificate roles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominee & Statuette: Songwriter(s) of new material. Publisher recognition as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 75 — Music Video (nominee/statuette/certificate roles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Category header present; specific nominee/statuette/certificate roles listed for Music Video/Film categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 76 — Music Film (nominee/statuette/certificate roles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominee & Statuette: Artist(s) of newly recorded material, Video Director(s) & Video Producer(s). Additional recognized roles: Audio Producer(s), Audio Mixer & Video Editor; distinctions for those with over 51% vs less than 51% playing time on music film.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statuette awarded to Artist(s) of newly recorded material, Video Director(s) & Video Producer(s) of over 51% of total playing time of music film; others with less than 51% may receive certificates or recognition as listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 77 — Recording Package (nominee/statuette/certificate roles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominee & Statuette: Art Director(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 78 — Album Cover (nominee/statuette/certificate roles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominee & Statuette: Art Director(s). Designer, Illustrator & Photographer may be recognized if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 79 — Album Notes (nominee/statuette/certificate roles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominee & Statuette: Album Notes Writer. No certificates issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of additional contributors (general album-category rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: For many album categories, additional contributors such as Featured Artist(s), Producer(s), Engineer/Mixer(s), Mastering Engineer(s), Immersive Producer(s) & Immersive Engineer/Mixer(s) may be recognized with certificates or statuettes depending on percentage of playing time (commonly >50%, >20%, or <50% thresholds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thresholds vary by category (examples: >50% playing time for many album categories; >20% for Album Of The Year roles; 33% for multi-composer video game scores).
